images.title: Use the whole number product
images.purpose: Show how a known whole number product gives a decimal product at once by counting decimal places.
images.composition: Two rows of working stacked in the centre, the whole number product on top and the decimal product below, with small count tags under the decimal numbers; one downward arrow links them.
exact_structure: One grey #6B7280 arrow pointing down from the top row to the bottom row.

Bottom row: "5.96 × 24.8 = 147.808"; in 5.96 the digits 9 and 6 after the point are teal #0072B2, in 24.8 the digit 8 after the point is amber #E69F00, and in 147.808 the 3 digits 8, 0, 8 after the point are reddish purple #CC79A7.
Under 5.96 a teal tag "2 places", under 24.8 an amber tag "1 place", under 147.808 a reddish purple tag "2 + 1 = 3 places".
rejection: the coloured digits after the point miscounted (not 2, 1 and 3)
the decimal point placed anywhere else in 147.808
images.takeaway: Remove the points, multiply, then give the product as many decimal places as both numbers together.
images.description: 596 × 248 = 147808 above, an arrow down to 5.96 × 24.8 = 147.808, with tags 2 places, 1 place and 2 + 1 = 3 places.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text that frames the rule from a known whole number product.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two rows digit by digit; only the position of the point changes.

image_decisions.why: Showing the two products aligned makes it clear that only the decimal point placement changes.
